economy.summary: Supports raising Pennsylvania's minimum wage from $7.25 to $15 an hour, saying it is wrong that the wage is stuck at $7.25 while the cost of groceries, gas, and utilities keeps going up, and urged the state Senate to take up the House-passed House Bill 2189.
economy.short: Supports raising state minimum wage to $15 an hour.

taxes.summary: His campaign site says he partnered across party lines to move state finances from budget deficits to surpluses and billions in the rainy day fund, supports a competitive tax structure to attract and retain employers, and is committed to maintaining property tax restraint, particularly for seniors.
taxes.short: Cites budget surpluses; supports property tax restraint for seniors.

abortion.summary: Advocated during December 2025 floor debate for a proposed state constitutional amendment protecting reproductive rights, arguing that Pennsylvania's existing abortion protections could be rolled back if Republicans won control of state government.
abortion.short: Supports state constitutional amendment protecting reproductive rights.

education.summary: His campaign site says he is focused on making public education funding more equitable in Pennsylvania to provide children with a quality education, and his campaign biography says he fought cuts to public education funding.
education.short: Supports more equitable public education funding; fought funding cuts.

healthcare.summary: His campaign biography says he has prioritized affordable and accessible health care during his time in office; the site does not detail specific healthcare proposals.
healthcare.short: Says he prioritizes affordable, accessible health care; no specifics.

energy.summary: Commended Governor Shapiro's 2025 energy plan for bringing together energy, labor, and environmental protection partners, and in November 2025 said Pennsylvania is not getting out of the Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative without taking care of its environment.
energy.short: Supports Shapiro energy plan; ties RGGI exit to environmental protection.

guns.summary: Supported the 2023 House-passed bills expanding background checks to all gun sales (House Bill 714) and creating a court-ordered process for temporary firearm removal (House Bill 1018), urged the state Senate to act on them, and called them the first meaningful gun safety legislation passed in nearly a decade.
guns.short: Supports universal background checks and temporary firearm removal law.
